To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rio Vista is an efficient and scalable recoverable-memory system.
Rio Vista is a recoverable memory library for Rio that achieves a speedup of 100-556x over standard recoverable memory systems.

(a) a 720-line library that does not use a redo log and does not use system calls can provide a 5-μsec transaction overhead and a 150-556× speedup for benchmarks based on the TPC-B and the TPC-C benchmarks; and (b) a 5- to 10-μsec transaction latency is fast enough for many applications, including transaction processing, database management, and distributed shared memory.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we design a file cache that is crash-safe? How can we design recoverable memories for crash-safe file caches? How can we use recoverable memories to implement high-performance transactions?

two questions: 1) Can we design a recoverable memory system that is fast enough to support transactions? 2) Can a recoverable memory library be designed that is efficient enough for transaction processing?
the question of how much overhead is necessary for a recoverable memory system to provide a high level of data consistency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the system described in this paper is a good example of how to use a combination of a file cache and a recoverable-memory library to improve the performance of transactions by a factor of thousands, while still providing the reliability and recoverability of conventional recoverable-memory systems.
Rio Vista is a very efficient and scalable transaction system that provides a very low overhead and very good performance.
this paper is a very interesting and well-written paper that presents a system that reduces the overhead of transactions by a factor of over 2000.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rio Vista system is a 150-556X improvement over the standard recoverable-memory model for applications with working sets that fit entirely in memory.
Rio Vista is a recoverable-memory system that provides the speed of a non-recoverable-memory system.
Rio-Vista is the first recoverable-memory system to provide a speedup of over 100x for a variety of benchmarks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the overhead of recoverable memory is not a fundamental barrier to its widespread use in transactional systems, and that recoverable memories can be made fast enough to support real-time applications.
a system that combines a high-performance file system with a high-performance recoverable-memory library can achieve performance that is comparable to that of a non-recoverable-memory system.
a small, carefully crafted, and highly optimized recoverable memory can achieve high performance.
